{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.4 (TrueLink Hosting, Interface and Support Agreement)

**To:** Deal team
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)
**Re:** Playbook review of EXHIBIT 10.4 — verified findings, deviations and next steps

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed EXHIBIT 10.4 against the playbook and produced 18 verified findings. The commercial architecture of the deal is, on the whole, favourable to us on the terms that most often cause trouble: there is no exclusivity, no non-compete, no minimum-purchase lock-in beyond a terminable 12-month floor, no non-solicit, no audit right against us, no liquidated damages, and no MFN burdening us (the only MFN runs in our favour on Hosting Services rates). Client has a unilateral termination-for-convenience right on roughly 30–60 days' notice with no exit fee, and the renewal mechanic (one-year terms, 30 days' notice by either party) meets our preferred position. Governing law and venue (California; San Luis Obispo County) sit at the fallback and are acceptable.

The problems are concentrated in risk allocation and in what the Agreement omits. Three clauses fail even the fallback and require redlines: the Vendor indemnity is limited to TrueLink's own breach and does not reach third-party IP infringement (with no non-infringement warranty anywhere to fill the gap); the liability cap is one-way, capping TrueLink at 12 months' hosting and support compensation while leaving Client — including under a broad Section 12a indemnity — entirely uncapped, which the playbook treats as walk-away territory; and TrueLink gives no performance warranty at all beyond a Year 2000 date-processing warranty, against a full disclaimer of implied warranties. Three further rules are outright missing for a vendor that hosts our site and processes consumer credit data: no insurance covenant of any kind, no confirmation that Client owns Client Content, Client IP and borrower data or the results of Support Services we pay for, and no post-termination transition assistance or data return/deletion. Assignment and licence scope are lower-severity deviations: no M&A successor carve-out and an unqualified consent standard on assignment, and a licence grant that reaches Client alone, with no route to affiliates or contractors.

Two commercial gaps should be closed before signature and are noted rather than flagged: the dollar minimums in Section 5a and the month figure in Section 4 are still blank, and Section 6 carves the minimum monthly fees out of our documentation and dispute rights.

We also note that Section 8(d) cross-references a separate Non-Competition Agreement governing Credit Data use. That instrument sits outside this review and should be reviewed separately, including for any personnel restrictions.

---

## 2. Findings table

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § 2 LICENSE. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 2 LICENSE. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY. |
| Medium | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | **Deviation** | § 12 INDEMNITY. |
| Medium | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality and carve-outs | **Deviation** | § 12 INDEMNITY. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant (at fallback) | § 12 INDEMNITY. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions | Compliant (at fallback) | § 5 COMPENSATION. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | Compliant | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY. |
| Low | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | § 12 INDEMNITY. |
| Low | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § 2 LICENSE. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | § 12 INDEMNITY. |
| Low | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Missing** | § 2 LICENSE. |
| Low | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | § 12 INDEMNITY. |

---

## 3. Deviations and missing clauses — what we changed and why

**INDEMN (§ 12) — deviation.** Section 12's TrueLink indemnity covers only breach by TrueLink of the Agreement or failure to perform its obligations. There is no TrueLink non-infringement warranty anywhere (Section 9 warranties are Year 2000 only; the infringement representations run from Client), so a breach-based indemnity does not reach third-party IP claims against the Interface or related software. Meanwhile Client's indemnity is broad and one-sided. Our redline inserts a concise TrueLink defence and indemnity covering third-party IP infringement (with Client Content and modification carve-outs), breach of law, data breach and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with notice, control and cooperation mechanics. *Verification returned fail — the insert must be re-run and re-validated before it goes out.*

**LOL-CAP (§ 12) — deviation.** The only cap protects TrueLink (12 months' hosting and support compensation); Client's liability, including under the Section 12a indemnity, is uncapped, and there is no mutual exclusion of indirect or consequential damages. A Vendor-only cap with the Customer uncapped is walk-away territory. We make the cap mutual at the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000, apply it to the Agreement as a whole, keep indemnification, confidentiality/data security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement outside the cap, and confirm Client's payment obligations are not capped liability. *Verification returned fail — re-run before circulation.*

**WARRANTY (§ 9, insert after p0060) — deviation.** TrueLink's only warranty is Year 2000 date processing. There is no professional/workmanlike warranty for the Hosting and Support Services, no conformance-to-documentation warranty, no compliance-with-laws or no-malicious-code warranty (those run only from Client), and no repair/replace/re-perform/refund remedy — all against a disclaimer of merchantability and fitness. That fails the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with remedies). Because the disclaimer is prefaced "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT," adding an express warranty suffices and no carve-out edit is needed. *Redline repaired and validated.*

**ASSIGN (§ 15) — deviation.** Section 15 bars assignment without prior written approval, with a sole exception for a "financially responsible affiliate." There is no successor/M&A carve-out (walk-away territory for a Customer assignment restriction) and the consent standard is unqualified. Helpfully, there is no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right anywhere. We add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Client, subject TrueLink's assignment to our consent (not unreasonably withheld) and bar assignment to a Client competitor, and confirm a Client change of control is not an assignment and gives TrueLink no exit. *Repaired and validated.*

**LICENSE (§ 2(a), with a conforming edit to § 15) — deviation.** The grant runs to Client alone; affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf are not licensed, and Section 2(b) adds only multi-site access. That fails the fallback (affiliates on written notice). The licence runs until termination rather than being revocable at will, which is acceptable. We add affiliates and contractors to the grant and successor transfer to Section 15. *Repaired and validated.*

**INSURANCE — missing.** No occurrence of "insurance" anywhere. TrueLink hosts our web site, operates the Interface and processes consumer credit data; no insurance at all for a vendor processing personal data is walk-away territory. We insert a new Section 31 (after Force Majeure, so existing numbering and the Section 24 survival reference are undisturbed) at preferred levels — CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request — with the E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M fallback offered in the comment. *Validated.*

**IP — missing.** Section 2(d) preserves TrueLink's rights in the Interface (acceptable), but nothing confirms Client retains title to Client Content, Client's Intellectual Property (defined but never operative) or borrower/loan data, and nothing addresses ownership of the results of the Support Services we pay for. Section 10(b)/(c) makes those items confidential, which is not ownership. We insert a reciprocal ownership subsection with assignment of Support Services deliverables and work product, a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to embedded TrueLink IP, and an express no-joint-ownership statement, expressed to be subject to the Section 8(d) Credit Data licence. *Repaired and validated.*

**TRANSITION — missing.** TrueLink holds Client Content and borrower/loan data, yet neither Section 13, Section 14 nor Section 10 gives us exit rights; Section 13 in fact puts the burden on Client to find a new name server within 30 days and new hosting within 60 days. There is no transition assistance, no data export in usable format and no deletion obligation. We insert Section 14a requiring transition assistance, return of Client data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion; it will survive under Section 24. *Repaired and validated.*

---

## 4. Walk-away items

These are the points the playbook classes as walk-away. We should not sign without movement on each:

1. **One-way liability cap (LOL-CAP, § 12).** A cap protecting only the Vendor while Client is uncapped — including under the broad Section 12a indemnity — is walk-away territory. Mutuality is non-negotiable; the quantum and carve-out list are where we can trade.
2. **No insurance whatsoever (INSURANCE).** For a vendor hosting our site and processing consumer credit data, the absence of any coverage requirement is walk-away territory. Fallback limits (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) are available.
3. **Assignment with no M&A successor carve-out (ASSIGN, § 15).** A Customer assignment restriction with no M&A carve-out is walk-away territory; as drafted, a merger or sale of substantially all our assets would need TrueLink's consent, on an unqualified standard.

We would also treat the combination of **no Vendor IP indemnity and no performance warranty of any kind** (INDEMN plus WARRANTY, against a full implied-warranty disclaimer) as an unacceptable risk position on this deal, even though neither rule is individually labelled walk-away.

---

## 5. Next steps

1. **Re-run and validate the INDEMN and LOL-CAP inserts.** Both currently show a failed verification. No redline goes to the counterparty until each is regenerated and validated.
2. **Circulate the validated redline package** covering WARRANTY, ASSIGN, LICENSE, INSURANCE (new Section 31), IP and TRANSITION (new Section 14a), with playbook-cited comments and, where noted above, the fallback offered on its face.
3. **Close the blanks with the business team.** Confirm the minimum monthly service fee figures in Section 5a and the minimum-period month figure in Section 4, and keep the Section 5a minimums modest. Separately, delete the Section 6 carve-out that excludes the minimum monthly fees from our documentation and dispute rights.
4. **Obtain and review the Non-Competition Agreement** cross-referenced at Section 8(d), including for any personnel or business restrictions that would change our EXCLUSIVITY, NONCOMPETE or NOSOLICIT conclusions.
5. **Prepare the negotiation sequence:** lead with the three walk-away items (mutual cap, insurance, M&A carve-out) plus the IP indemnity and performance warranty; hold the lower-severity licence-scope and ownership inserts as a package we can close quickly once the risk-allocation points land.
6. **Do not spend leverage** on the items we have classified compliant — governing law/venue at the California fallback, the 30-day (rather than 90-day) non-renewal notice, the absence of a renewal reminder or price cap, or the terminable minimum monthly floor. Each is acceptable as drafted, and several run in our favour.

*Note for the record: the Vendor MFN in Section 6 on Hosting Services rates has no audit or true-up mechanic. That is an enhancement we may raise opportunistically, not a deviation.*"}
